issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 03/08/26

✅ Implementation: Add Text Wall Picture to Viewer JSON

Files Changed

  • src/action/v1/exhibition/getExhibitionDetail.go
  • src/action/v1/exhibition/getViewerJSON.go
  • src/action/v1/exhibition/getViewerJSON_test.go

Implementation Summary

The viewer JSON text wall mapping now includes the existing text_wall.picture column. This makes picture available in exhibition.text_walls[] for GET /v1/viewers/json/:sid and any rebuild path that uses the same viewer payload builder.

Because GET /v1/viewers/json/:sid can serve an older viewer.json file from disk when json_version has not changed, the endpoint now also detects stale text wall payloads that do not contain the picture key and rebuilds them from DB.

Code Changes

  1. Added picture to the text wall response struct:
type textWallItem struct {
	ID      interface{} `json:"id"`
	Name    string      `json:"name"`
	Content string      `json:"content"`
	Color   string      `json:"color"`
	Picture *string     `json:"picture"`
	// existing fields continue here
}
  1. Included picture in the text wall query:
Select(strings.Join([]string{
	"id",
	"exhibition_id",
	"name",
	"content",
	"color",
	"picture",
	"font_size",
	// existing columns continue here
}, ", "))
  1. Mapped the model field into the response item:
resp = append(resp, textWallItem{
	ID:      t.ID,
	Name:    t.Name,
	Content: t.Content,
	Color:   t.Color,
	Picture: t.Picture,
	// existing fields continue here
})
  1. Added stale viewer-file detection in GetViewerJSON:
if (strings.TrimSpace(meta.JsonVersion) != "" && meta.JsonVersion != oldVersion) || viewerNeedsTextWallPictureRebuild(viewer) {
	viewer, rawViewerB64, err = RebuildViewerPayload(meta, sid)
	// write rebuilt viewer.json and update Redis
}
  1. Added viewerNeedsTextWallPictureRebuild:
func viewerNeedsTextWallPictureRebuild(viewer map[string]any) bool {
	exhibition, ok := viewer["exhibition"].(map[string]any)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	textWalls, ok := exhibition["text_walls"].([]any)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	for _, textWall := range textWalls {
		tw, ok := textWall.(map[string]any)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		if _, ok := tw["picture"]; !ok {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
  1. Added unit coverage for stale and current payload detection:
func TestViewerNeedsTextWallPictureRebuild(t *testing.T)
func TestViewerNeedsTextWallPictureRebuildAllowsNullPicture(t *testing.T)

Behavior

GET /v1/viewers/json/:sid now returns:

{
  "exhibition": {
    "text_walls": [
      {
        "id": "...",
        "name": "...",
        "content": "...",
        "color": "...",
        "picture": "user/exhibition/textwall/file.png"
      }
    ]
  }
}

If a text wall has no stored picture, picture is returned as null. Existing disk files that were generated before this field existed are rebuilt automatically on the next viewer JSON request.

Verification

Run:

gofmt -w src/action/v1/exhibition/getExhibitionDetail.go src/action/v1/exhibition/getViewerJSON.go src/action/v1/exhibition/getViewerJSON_test.go
go test ./src/action/v1/exhibition

Expected result:

ok  	villume-backend-go/src/action/v1/exhibition

Overview

Endpoint GET /v1/viewers/json/:sid should include the picture field for each text wall object in the viewer JSON payload. The field already exists in the text_wall table and is used by text wall upload/save flows, but it was missing from the viewer response.

Problem

The viewer JSON builder returned exhibition.text_walls without picture, so clients could not render text wall image assets from /v1/viewers/json/:sid.

Root Cause

The shared text wall response mapping did not include the picture column:

  1. fetchTextWallsByExhibitionID did not select picture from text_wall.
  2. textWallItem did not define a picture JSON field.
  3. mapTextWallsToResponse did not copy models.TextWall.Picture into the response.

Implementation

Updated src/action/v1/exhibition/getExhibitionDetail.go to:

  1. Add Picture *string to textWallItem with JSON key picture.
  2. Include picture in the text_wall select list.
  3. Map t.Picture into each text wall response item.

Scope

In scope:

  • GET /v1/viewers/json/:sid
  • exhibition.text_walls[].picture in viewer JSON rebuild/response flow
  • Existing text wall DB field text_wall.picture

Out of scope:

  • Text wall upload behavior
  • Database schema changes
  • Route changes
  • Response changes outside text wall objects

Acceptance Criteria

  1. GET /v1/viewers/json/:sid includes picture for each item in exhibition.text_walls.
  2. picture is null when no picture is stored.
  3. Existing text wall fields remain unchanged.
  4. Code is formatted with gofmt.
  5. go test ./src/action/v1/exhibition passes.

Verification

RESULT 09/07/26

✅ Implementation: Fix List Coupon

Files Changed

  • src/action/v1/billing/coupon/listCoupon.go

Implementation Summary

The ListCoupon action now delegates DB promo-id retrieval to helper functions and uses a versioned Redis key for the list cache. It also keeps an in-memory guard while enriching coupons from Stripe so duplicate promo_id values cannot be appended to the response.

Code Changes

  1. Updated the Redis cache key call:
cacheKey := redis.Key.BillingCouponList(redis.BillingCouponListParams{
	Limit:    limit,
	Page:     page,
	IsActive: activeQuery,
}, 2)

This moves the list endpoint to coupon-list cache version 2, preventing old cached payloads from the earlier implementation from being reused.

  1. Extracted promo-id lookup into listCouponPromoIDs:
func listCouponPromoIDs(db *gorm.DB, activeQuery string, limit int, offset int) ([]string, int64, error) {
	query := listCouponPromoIDQuery(db, activeQuery)

	var total int64
	if err := query.Count(&total).Error; err != nil {
		return nil, 0, err
	}

	var promoIDs []string
	if err := query.
		Order("MAX(updated_at) DESC, promo_id DESC").
		Limit(limit).
		Offset(offset).
		Pluck("promo_id", &promoIDs).Error; err != nil {
		return nil, 0, err
	}

	return promoIDs, total, nil
}
  1. Extracted grouped query construction into listCouponPromoIDQuery:
func listCouponPromoIDQuery(db *gorm.DB, activeQuery string) *gorm.DB {
	query := db.Table("coupon").
		Select("promo_id").
		Where("promo_id IS NOT NULL AND promo_id <> ?", "").
		Group("promo_id")

	if activeQuery != "" {
		query = query.Where("active = ?", activeQuery)
	}

	return query
}
  1. Added a defensive duplicate guard before Stripe enrichment:
seenPromoIDs := map[string]struct{}{}
for _, promoID := range promoIDs {
	if _, exists := seenPromoIDs[promoID]; exists {
		continue
	}
	seenPromoIDs[promoID] = struct{}{}

	// Stripe promotion-code lookup continues here.
}

Behavior

The endpoint still reads local coupon rows first, then retrieves each Stripe promotion code with coupon expanded. The response shape is unchanged. The fix only changes how promo IDs are selected, deduplicated, and cached.

Verification

Run:

go test ./src/action/v1/billing/coupon

Expected result:

?   	villume-backend-go/src/action/v1/billing/coupon	[no test files]

Overview

Endpoint GET /v1/billing/coupons has a bug in list generation and cache behavior. The endpoint is used by support/admin users to fetch coupon promotion codes from the local coupon table, enrich each row with Stripe promotion-code data, and return a paginated response.

Problems

The previous ListCoupon flow mixed request parsing, cache handling, DB querying, Stripe enrichment, and response shaping in one large function. It also queried coupon rows directly enough that duplicate promo_id values could leak into the Stripe lookup loop and response, and the Redis cache key used the default cache version, which could keep older cached payloads alive after the response shape changed.

Goals

  1. Keep authorization behavior unchanged: users with role user still receive 401 Unauthorized.
  2. Keep query parameters unchanged:
    • limit, default 10
    • page, default 1
    • is_active, optional filter
  3. Build the coupon list from distinct non-empty promo_id values.
  4. Keep pagination and total count based on the grouped promo_id query.
  5. Avoid duplicate promotion-code processing in the response assembly.
  6. Move DB promo-id lookup into small helper functions so the controller action is easier to read and test.
  7. Version the Redis list cache key to avoid stale payloads from the older implementation.
  8. Keep existing response contract:
    • total
    • list_coupon
    • last_login
    • encrypt
    • coupon fields such as name, code, discount, active, type_discount, expires, used, duration, duration_in_months, created_at, metadata, and encoded promo_id.

Scope

In scope:

  • src/action/v1/billing/coupon/listCoupon.go
  • Redis list cache key usage for ListCoupon
  • DB helper functions for distinct promo-id query

Out of scope:

  • Route changes
  • Request/response schema changes
  • Stripe create/edit/delete coupon behavior
  • Database schema or migration changes
  • API collection changes

Acceptance Criteria

  1. GET /v1/billing/coupons returns the same payload structure as before.
  2. Duplicate promo_id values are not processed more than once.
  3. is_active filter still applies when provided.
  4. Empty or null promo_id rows are ignored.
  5. Cache key uses coupon-list cache version 2.
  6. Code compiles with go test ./src/action/v1/billing/coupon.

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 07/07/26

✅ Implementation: Fix Coupon Detail Cache Invalidation Bug

Resolution Strategy

To resolve the caching issue outlined in the task, the targeted cache invalidation logic—which was already properly implemented in the deleteCoupon.go API—was brought over to the editCoupon.go API.

Code Changes

The following modifications were made in src/action/v1/billing/coupon/editCoupon.go:

  1. Added Import: Imported the "encoding/base64" package to allow for the encoding of the Stripe Promo ID.
  2. Explicit Cache Deletion: After a successful update of the coupon both in the database and on Stripe, the Stripe promo_id is base64-encoded to generate the encodedSid.
  3. Trigger Invalidation: The exact cache key for the detail API is explicitly deleted by invoking redis.Delete(c.Context(), redis.Key.CouponDetail(encodedSid)). This is done directly before deleting the broader BillingCouponPattern.

Code Diff Snippet

import (
+	"encoding/base64"
	"errors"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// ... (within the EditCoupon function)

	// 4. Update Coupon in DB
	if err := config.DB.Table("coupon").
		Where("code = ?", codeParam).
		Updates(map[string]interface{}{
			"name":       nameCoupon,
			"updated_at": time.Now(),
		}).Error; err != nil {
		return helpers.SendError(c, helpers.ErrorOpts{Status: fiber.StatusConflict, Messages: "Failed to update coupon in database"})
	}

+	encodedSid := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(promoID))
+	_ = redis.Delete(c.Context(), redis.Key.CouponDetail(encodedSid))
	_ = redis.DeletePattern(c.Context(), redis.Key.BillingCouponPattern())

Outcome

By manually flushing the CouponDetail cache key, the detail endpoint is forced to fetch the freshly updated coupon data directly from Stripe and the database upon its next invocation following any edit. This rectifies the stale data bug immediately.

Overview

A bug was discovered in the coupon billing APIs where editing a coupon via the editCoupon API correctly updates the name in the database and on Stripe, but the changes are not reflected when subsequently calling the detailCoupon API. The detail API continued to return the old, stale coupon name.

Root Cause Analysis

The issue stems from incorrect Redis cache invalidation within the editCoupon API.

  1. Detail API Caching Mechanism:
    The detailCoupon API fetches data from Stripe/DB and caches the response for 24 hours. The cache key used for this is redis.Key.CouponDetail(sid), which translates to a format like [PREFIX]:coupon:v[VERSION]:detail:[SID]. The sid in this context is the base64-encoded Stripe promo_id.

  2. Edit API Cache Clearing Mechanism:
    Upon a successful update, the editCoupon API attempts to clear the coupon-related caches by calling redis.DeletePattern(..., redis.Key.BillingCouponPattern()).
    The BillingCouponPattern() yields the pattern [PREFIX]:billing:*:coupons:*.

  3. The Mismatch:
    Because [PREFIX]:billing:*:coupons:* does not match the cache key pattern [PREFIX]:coupon:v[VERSION]:detail:[SID], the specific cache entry for the detailed coupon is never flushed. Thus, subsequent calls to the detailCoupon API return a cache HIT containing the stale data until the 24-hour TTL expires.

Implementation

The implementation details for this fix have been documented separately.

✅ Implementation: Standardize API Response Format

Reference Commit: 2f4b1a5

Overview

Standardize all API responses across the Villume backend to conform strictly to the legacy/client expected API envelope contract. The refactoring unifies both plaintext and encrypted success envelopes, standardizes error envelopes, replaces legacy singular message keys with uniform messages keys, introduces delimiters for field-specific error binding (| for input errors, || for metadata tags), and maps HTTP status codes into standardized uppercase status strings (BAD_REQUEST, UNAUTHENTICATED, CONFLICT, etc.).
